faq.a: Nine: Pre-Listing, Pre-Contract, Active Listing, Under Contract, Option Period, Inspection, Financing, Title & Survey, and Clear to Close. A tenth stage, Closed, exists in the data model but is shown in a separate Closed Dossiers view rather than as a column on the board.
faq.q: What stages does the Pipeline Dashboard track?

faq.a: Each card shows its nearest upcoming deadline pulled from that dossier's contract-derived dates. If none is set, it falls back to the closing date, marked overdue in red if that date has already passed.
faq.q: How does Dossie decide which deadline to show on a card?

faq.a: No. Once a dossier is archived, it's removed from the Pipeline board and appears instead under Closed Dossiers in the side navigation, which keeps a running count of how many files are archived.
faq.q: Do closed deals stay on the Pipeline board?

faq.a: Yes. Opening any dossier gives the option to advance it to the next stage or move it directly to a specific stage, in addition to the automatic progression as the deal moves forward.
faq.q: Can I move a deal to a different stage manually?

deck: Nine stages, one board, every open file visible at a glance. Dossie's Pipeline Dashboard is the home screen for an agent's whole book of business — no spreadsheet, no separate tracker.

steps.p: Pre-Listing, Pre-Contract, Active Listing, Under Contract, Option Period, Inspection, Financing, Title & Survey, and Clear to Close each get their own column. A dossier moves left to right as the deal progresses; nothing has to be re-entered or re-filed to change columns.

steps.h: 2. Each card shows what's next, not just what's open
steps.p: Every card carries the property address (or client names if the address isn't set yet), the counterparty, and the nearest upcoming deadline. A deadline within 3 days shows red, within 7 days shows amber, and anything further out shows neutral — so the board itself tells an agent where to look first without opening a single file.

steps.h: 3. Closed files move off the board on their own
steps.p: Once a dossier is archived at Clear to Close, it drops out of the Pipeline board entirely and moves into its own Closed Dossiers view in the side nav — so the active board only ever shows deals that still need attention, never a growing pile of finished ones.

title: How Dossie Handles the Pipeline Dashboard
callout: The board also carries two quiet signals beyond the stage columns: a trophy badge on any dossier with a closing milestone card ready to share, and an envelope badge on any file where a compliance document packet has already gone out — both visible without opening the dossier.
